clue.text: A section of a party around North getting coverage?

indicators.note: around says the wing of the party wraps itself about the compass letter

parts.note: a wing is a faction or section of a political party

explanation.surface: Part of a political party gathers round its northern members and wins press attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coverage' suggests media attention, but an awning gives literal cover overhead; the question mark flags the shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas sheet over a shopfront or window provides shelter, a kind of overhead protection.

clue.text: Communist almost invading a business district, a terrible act

indicators.note: invading says the shortened communist goes into the middle of the district

parts.note: the City is London's financial district

indicators.note: almost says the final letter of the left-winger's nickname is dropped

parts.note: Trot is a short form of Trotskyist, used loosely for a communist

explanation.surface: A communist infiltrates London's financial quarter and commits an outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TROT to TRO; the CITY is London's square-mile financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity is an appalling, wicked deed, exactly a terrible act.

clue.text: Other chef cooking around back of kitchen from now

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters surround the single letter from the kitchen
cooking says the letters of the two words are worked up into a new arrangement
back of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A second chef busy at the stove, moving around the back of the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' gives HECEFORTH, which goes 'around' the 'back of kitchen'; 'chef cooking' reads like a kitchen scene but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Henceforth is a formal adverb meaning from this time onwards.

clue.text: Speed is hazard traversing black loch

indicators.note: traversing says the hazard lies across the gap between colour and lake

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
Loch Ness is the most famous Scottish loch
a hazard is a risk

explanation.surface: Going fast is dangerous when crossing a dark Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link here. Loch NESS is the Scottish lake of monster fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Briskness is quickness and liveliness of movement, a synonym for speed.

clue.text: Trim container for ammunition

definitions.meaning: to trim is to cut short, as with shears
a magazine holding cartridges that is loaded into a gun

explanation.surface: Cut back the box of bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: To clip is to cut or trim; a clip also holds cartridges for a firearm.

clue.text: Agents detaining dishonourable fellow, chirpy type

indicators.note: detaining says the agency holds the scoundrel inside it

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, a body of agents
a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably

explanation.surface: Spies hold a scoundrel who turns out to be cheerfully talkative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chirpy' sounds like a cheerful person, but this insect literally chirps.
explanation.definitionFit: The cicada is an insect famous for its loud chirping song.

clue.text: Try huge walkabout round middle of jungles to see gorillas' behaviour?

indicators.note: round says the shuffled letters encircle the single central letter
walkabout suggests the letters wandering into a new order
middle of picks the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A suggestion to take a long trek through the jungle to watch gorillas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walkabout' gives THUGERY, which goes 'round' the 'middle of jungles'. Gorillas here are thugs, not apes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorilla is slang for a hired heavy, so their conduct is violent bullying.

clue.text: Sign in west obscured by sun

indicators.note: obscured says the letters are disguised by being rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: A signal in the western sky hidden by the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscured' turns IN WEST into WITNES; 'by' links on the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness a document is to sign it as an observer of another's signature.

clue.text: Identify awkward situation

definitions.meaning: to identify is to pick out or notice
a tricky fix, as in being in a tight corner

explanation.surface: Pick out a tricky predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot is to notice or recognise; a tight spot is a difficult position.

clue.text: Explorer with outfit imbibing drink in front of hotel

indicators.note: in front of places the first piece ahead of the hotel letter
imbibing says the outfit swallows the drink inside it

parts.note: a rig is an outfit of clothes
ale is a drink, beer
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An adventurer in his gear drinks a beer at the front of the hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Walter RALEIGH was the Elizabethan explorer and courtier.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was an English adventurer who sailed to the Americas.

clue.text: Decrease vote for military award

parts.note: read as de-crease: to iron is to remove creases
a cross is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Lower the ballot count to fund a medal for soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decrease' reads as 'de-crease', what an IRON does; a CROSS is how a British voter marks the ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Cross was a German decoration for bravery in war.

clue.text: Shot along in Grand Prix from the back producing damage to car

indicators.note: in says the running piece sits inside the motor-race letters
from the back says the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: GP is the abbreviation for Grand Prix
to shoot along is to run, so ran

explanation.surface: Racing along in a Formula One event and ending up crashing the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the back' gives PG, which takes the running piece inside. PRANG is British slang for a minor car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is British slang for a crash or the dent it leaves in a vehicle.

clue.text: Trouble close to raging fire out of control

indicators.note: close to picks the last letter of the word
out of control says the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Disaster as a raging blaze spreads unchecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of control' turns FIRE into RIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief can mean trouble or annoyance, as in giving someone grief.

clue.text: Lunatic in cycling helmet?

definitions.meaning: a protective shell for the head, playfully read as a holder for one's nut

explanation.surface: A madman in a bike hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutcase is a crazy person; jokingly, it is a case for your nut, or head.

clue.text: Outing to take in endlessly dissolute chap and awful singer

indicators.note: to take in says the trip encloses the pieces that follow

parts.note: a tour is an outing or trip

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter of the rake is dropped

parts.note: a roue is a debauched man, a rake
bad means awful

explanation.surface: A trip that includes a debauched man and a dreadful vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful singer' looks like one phrase, but 'awful' is BAD and 'singer' alone defines; ROUE loses its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A troubadour was a medieval lyric poet who sang his verses.

clue.text: Brief sale planned for artistic work

indicators.note: planned says the letters are organised into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A short-lived auction arranged to sell a piece of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Bas-relief is low-relief sculpture, carving that projects slightly from its background.

clue.text: Value considerably parking facility around Harrods, say

indicators.note: around says the roadside stopping place wraps the shop

parts.note: a lay-by is a roadside area for parking off a main road
Harrods is an example of a great store

explanation.surface: Rate highly the car park around a famous London shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A LAY-BY is a British roadside pull-in; HARRODS is London's famous Knightsbridge department store.
explanation.definitionFit: To set great store by something is to prize it highly, an idiom for valuing.

clue.text: Foolish person left for daughter cosmetic accessory

indicators.note: for says one letter stands in place of the other

parts.note: dipstick is slang for a stupid person

explanation.surface: A silly person leaves in place of her daughter, taking her makeup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left for daughter' means put L where D was in DIPSTICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipstick is a stick of colour applied to the lips as makeup.

clue.text: Hasten start of punt in river before change in tide

indicators.note: before puts the river piece ahead of the reworked tide
in says the opening letter goes inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of the word
change in says the letters of the word are altered in order

explanation.surface: Hurry to get a punt onto the river before the tide turns.
explanation.walkthrough: The EXE is a river in south-west England. 'change in' turns TIDE into DITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite is to speed something up, to hasten it.

clue.text: Baseball player's means to carry liquid

definitions.meaning: the player who throws to the batter
a large jug for pouring water or milk

explanation.surface: The baseball thrower's water jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitcher throws the ball in baseball; a pitcher is also a jug.

clue.text: Greek character restricted trick in house

parts.note: tau is the Greek letter T

indicators.note: restricted says the word is cut short at its end

parts.note: a ruse is a trick

explanation.surface: A Greek man pulls a limited trick at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is an astrological house: a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus, the bull, is one of the twelve zodiac signs, called houses in astrology.

clue.text: Man say getting offer to include exercise

indicators.note: to include says the offer contains the exercise letters

parts.note: a bid is an offer
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: A man makes an offer that includes a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans walk on two legs, so a man is an example of a two-footed creature.

clue.text: Rob front of office in port

indicators.note: in says the opening letter goes into the port

parts.note: Dover is a Channel port in Kent

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Burgle the front office in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: DOVER is England's main Channel ferry port; DO OVER is British slang for burgle.
explanation.definitionFit: To do over is British slang for burgling a place or beating someone up.

clue.text: Some top assists, common feature of a football game

definitions.text: common feature of a football game

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the best assists are a regular part of a football match.
explanation.definitionFit: Kicking the ball to a teammate is a basic move in every soccer match.

clue.text: Suit maybe beginning to tangle beside bottom

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the word

parts.note: the rump is the bottom or buttocks

explanation.surface: A suit, perhaps, starting to tangle around the backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing, but it is a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the trump suit outranks the others, so it is one example of a suit.

clue.text: Idea from timeless factory

indicators.note: timeless says the time letter is taken away

parts.note: a plant is a factory

explanation.surface: A concept from a timeless factory.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the usual abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scheme or idea for doing something.

clue.text: Welsh place left secure beside rough mound miles away

parts.note: to land is to secure, as a catch or contract

indicators.note: rough says the remaining letters are roughed up into a new order
away says the miles letter is taken out

explanation.surface: A place in Wales: left secure beside a rough mound miles away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' takes M from MOUND, then 'rough' turns OUND into UDNO. LLANDUDNO is a seaside resort in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Llandudno is a Victorian seaside resort town on the north Wales coast.

clue.text: Salvation Army blocks unrefined moral campaign

indicators.note: blocks says the army sits inside the word, blocking it

parts.note: crude means unrefined, as in oil

explanation.surface: The Salvation Army obstructs a vulgar campaign for virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade is a vigorous campaign for a cause, often a reforming one.

clue.text: Travel regularly with second tiny building let out

parts.note: a hut is a small, simple building

indicators.note: out says the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Commuting with a small shed rented out on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns LET into TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To shuttle is to travel back and forth on a regular route.
